summary: Comments on the File Transfer Protocol. It is an old version of the discussion and was replaced by RFC 624, with related views in RFCs 614, 542 and 640.

eli5.summary: A person listed ideas to improve the file-transfer rules. A newer version of the same comments replaced this one.

questions: what changes did rfc 607 propose for ftp
what is the ftp actv command
subtitle: A 1974 list of thirteen quick fixes that would make the File Transfer Protocol easier to implement.

tldr.problem: The authors found that the FTP of the time had drawbacks that made user and server programs more complicated than necessary, especially in reply handling.
tldr.mechanism: They list thirteen problems with proposed solutions, such as same-length command verbs, a single success reply digit, a fixed ordering of replies and limits on line lengths.
tldr.outcome: This memo was obsoleted by RFC 624 and updated by RFC 614.

today: RFC 607 has been obsoleted by RFC 624 and was updated by RFC 614, so it is a historical set of comments on early FTP.

sections.title: Purpose of the Comments
sections.content: The authors say the File Transfer Protocol has several serious drawbacks. Some are basic and would need substantial design changes, which they promise to discuss in a later RFC. This memo covers problems that could be remedied with very little effort, each with a proposed solution.
sections.eli5: Some problems are big and need a redesign. This list only has the small ones that can be fixed quickly.

sections.title: Command and Handshake Fixes
sections.content:
Items 1 to 4 and 8 address commands and ordering. A new ACTV command would let a server that was told to be passive become active again. The three-letter BYE would become a four-letter verb such as QUIT, with all future verbs four letters long. The server would send the 250 reply before trying to open the data connection, so the user knows what to wait for.

A server that skips an unneeded command such as ACCT or ALLO must return a success reply, not an error. In blocked mode, data between the final end-of-record marker and end of file would be discarded.
sections.eli5: Make all the command words the same length, say things in a set order, and do not call it an error when a computer simply does not need a step.

sections.title: Simplifying Replies
sections.content:
Items 6, 7 and 9 to 12 aim to make reply parsing simple for user programs. The authors want a unique reply code, such as 009, for all lines of a multi-line reply after the first, and a maximum nesting level for multi-line replies. They ask that every success reply begin with one unique digit such as 2, with finer meaning in later digits, and that replies meant only for humans begin with another unique digit such as 0. Item 5 asks for maximum lengths for TELNET lines, user names, passwords, account numbers and pathnames, to be set after polling serving sites.

Item 13 suggests that reply code 331 listed as a success reply for several commands is probably a typographical error for 332 LOGIN FIRST, PLEASE.
sections.eli5: If every good answer started with the same number, a program could tell success from failure at a glance.
